clue.text: It's painful to catch something hairy

parts.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it
a tache is a moustache, a hairy growth on the lip

explanation.surface: Someone warns that grabbing hold of a hairy creature will hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief or deep sorrow is a painful emotional state, so the phrase describes it fairly.

clue.text: Rough dog

definitions.meaning: a hoarse, rasping voice is described this way
a sled dog breed of the Arctic

explanation.surface: A dog with a coarse coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, hoarse voice and an Arctic sled dog share this word.

clue.text: A paper in dispute

parts.note: tissue is a thin soft paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper caught up in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter under debate or argument is said to be the subject being contested, an idiom for in dispute.

clue.text: Delight, as contestant finally was in control of game

indicators.note: the closing letter of contestant

parts.note: to run something is to be in control of it
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: A contestant delighted to end up controlling a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport in the sense of rapture or ecstasy is a strong form of delight.

clue.text: A dash of old port, suggestion after hot beverage

indicators.note: the port and suggestion come after the tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
a trace is a slight suggestion or hint

explanation.surface: A splash of vintage port and a hint of something follow a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A dash of old port' looks like a drink, but 'A dash of old' is the definition: an ancient race.
explanation.definitionFit: Chariot races were ancient Roman sprints, so they were a dash of former times.

clue.text: Self-esteem to depart after low grade

indicators.note: the departing word comes after the grade letter

parts.note: E is a low grade in exams
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: Confidence leaves after a poor exam mark.
explanation.definitionFit: One's ego is one's sense of self-worth, a synonym for self-esteem.

clue.text: Round in possible semicircle, then march to the left

parts.note: the capital letter D has a semicircular shape

indicators.note: in an across answer, going to the left means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A geometry instruction: draw a semicircle and then move leftwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the left' reverses the march (OMED); a capital D looks like half a circle, hence 'possible'.
explanation.definitionFit: A domed roof is rounded on top, so round as an adjective is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Look for water, quantity around opening in well

indicators.note: the measured quantity goes around the initial letter

parts.note: a dose is a measured quantity

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word well

explanation.surface: Searching for water by measuring an amount around the mouth of a well.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowsing is searching for underground water with a rod, so it means look for water.

clue.text: Drink in vermouth, stuff from the South

indicators.note: in a down answer, reading from the bottom up reverses the pieces

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A drink containing vermouth and something from southern parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the South' reads INITRAM upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth, so it is an example of a drink.

clue.text: Recognised and understood, order rescinded

indicators.note: the letters of rescinded are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone realised and grasped that an order had been cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to perceive and grasp, so the past tense means recognised and understood.

clue.text: A tapering object secures a plant

indicators.note: the spire holds the small word a firmly within its letters

parts.note: a spire tapers to a point atop a church

explanation.surface: A pointed stake is used to hold a plant in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiraea is a genus of flowering shrubs, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Covering two directions, roads moving ahead

indicators.note: the rearranged roads wrap around the two compass points
the letters of roads are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: N and W are the compass points north and west

explanation.surface: Roads heading forward in two compass directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the roads to OARDS; 'Covering' then has them wrap the two directions, the O staying outside at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving onwards means going forward, so ahead as an adverb is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Those in agreement may celebrate as the process ends

parts.note: someone celebrating might shout yes

indicators.note: the final letters of the words the and process

explanation.surface: Supporters of a motion cheer when the procedure finally finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Affirmative votes or replies are those agreeing, so the plural noun names them.

clue.text: Engrossed in easier novel, reading Hebrew

indicators.note: the reading matter sits absorbed inside the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters of easier take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: lit is short for literature, reading matter

explanation.surface: Someone finds a more accessible novel absorbing to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' is the anagram signal, not a book; it yields ISRAEE, and 'Engrossed in' places the reading matter before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israelite was a member of the ancient Hebrew people, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Send round doctor, worried getting chill

indicators.note: the sending word goes round the tampering word

parts.note: to refer is to send someone on, as to a specialist
to doctor or rig is to tamper with
ate in the sense of what's eating you, worried at

explanation.surface: A patient referred to a doctor, anxious about catching a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb here, RIG, not a GP.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrigerate food is to chill it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Reminder line must be read out?

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word for a waiting line matches the reminder

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: An actor told that a line of the script must be spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an actor's line, but the line is a queue of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue prompts an actor or performer to act, so it is a reminder.

clue.text: Something sharp in toothed device spotted — like this?

definitions.text: Something sharp in toothed device spotted — like this?

indicators.note: the sharp item is placed within the toothed wheel

parts.note: a cog is a toothed wheel
a pin is something sharp
saw is the past tense of see, so spotted

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a sharp object inside a toothed tool, and wonders what it was.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a sharp, toothed cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A coping saw is a fine-bladed toothed tool for cutting curves, a sharp toothed device.

clue.text: Broken down, where in France to camp?

parts.note: où is French for where
a camp is a faction or group within a party

explanation.surface: A broken-down vehicle in France, and the driver wondering where to pitch a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that has broken down is not working, the idiom for which this phrase is.

clue.text: Party having come together, toed the line

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative Party
something formed has come together

explanation.surface: A political party unites and its members fall into line.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to comply with rules, so the past tense matches the idiom toed the line.

clue.text: Backward-looking leading nation cut adrift for periods in Washington, say?

indicators.note: the word for leading is read in reverse

parts.note: a team leading is up

indicators.note: cut adrift, the letters of nation cut float into a new order

explanation.surface: A once-dominant country, now looking back, has been cast off for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward-looking' turns UP into PU; 'adrift' rearranges NATIONCUT into NCTUATION. Americans call full stops periods.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a full stop is a period, and full stops are marks of this kind of writing system.

clue.text: Those missing food, topside of beef gone?

parts.note: nosh is slang for food

indicators.note: the top letter of the beef word, in a down answer
the top letter is removed

parts.note: cows are beef cattle

explanation.surface: People going without food, the joint of beef having disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topside' is a cut of beef, but here it is the top of COWS, deleted to leave OWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Absentees who fail to turn up are people missing an event, the noun for those.

clue.text: Sixties youth defending government department

definitions.meaning: a member of the 1960s British youth culture known for scooters and sharp suits

explanation.surface: A young person from the 1960s protecting a ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the same three letters: a 1960s subculture member and the defence ministry's abbreviation.

clue.text: Great enthusiasm bedding house plant

indicators.note: the enthusiasm word beds the house abbreviation within it

parts.note: a mania is a great enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A gardener with great enthusiasm bedding out a houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house plant' reads as one item, but 'house' is HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahonia is an evergreen shrub with yellow flowers, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Lazily pose with relative crossing over bridge, say

indicators.note: the relative straddles the rearranged letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a niece is a family relative

indicators.note: posed lazily, the letters of pose slump into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone poses idly with a family member walking across a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lazily' gives OSEP; 'crossing over' has the relative straddle it. The bridge is the part of spectacles resting on the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The bridge of a pair of spectacles rests on the nose, and is an example of this part.

clue.text: Blooming thing like modern music

definitions.meaning: pop music style, catchy and chart-friendly

explanation.surface: A flower compared to contemporary music.
explanation.definitionFit: A red flower and an adjective meaning catchy, in the style of pop, share this word.

clue.text: Alternative to the round brackets

indicators.note: the words to the round enclose the answer's letters between them, as brackets hold text

explanation.surface: A suggestion for something to use in place of parentheses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round brackets' looks like a punctuation phrase, but 'round' is part of the hiding place and 'brackets' alone says the answer is held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Another option is a different choice, so the adjective is a synonym of alternative.

clue.text: Observation regarding capacity and energy

parts.note: re means regarding
cc, cubic centimetres, measures engine capacity
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A remark about how much something holds and how much power it has.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce is a reconnaissance, a mission of military observation.

clue.text: Cork goalie

definitions.meaning: a cork is a bung that seals a bottle
a goalkeeper's job is to block shots

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper from the Irish city of Cork.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung plugging a bottle and a keeper blocking shots both share the one noun.

clue.text: Judge rarely enjoying football, all kicking off

indicators.note: each of the three words gives its kick-off letter

explanation.surface: A judge who seldom likes football, with everyone starting a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee judges play on the field, so the short form fits judge.

clue.text: Book unfortunately unfinished, fellow opening it

indicators.note: the man opens up the shortened word, sitting inside it
the last letter of the regretful word is dropped

parts.note: alack is an old exclamation of regret, meaning unfortunately
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man begins to read a book that, sadly, was never completed.
explanation.walkthrough: Alack is an archaic cry of regret; 'unfinished' leaves ALAC, and 'opening it' means the fellow opens that shortened word up.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual reference book, so it is an example of a book.

clue.text: Fine with children's game

parts.note: I spy is a guessing game played by children

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to go along with a game for kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Wispy hair is fine and thin, so the adjectives are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Retrieve food for bird

parts.note: in cricket, to field is to retrieve the ball after a hit
fare is food served

explanation.surface: An instruction to fetch something for a bird to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: To field, in cricket, is to stop and return a struck ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a large thrush that winters in Britain, an example of a bird.
